newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tunis Air 737 freighter to start Paris service.
newsitem.headline: Tunis Air 737 freighter to start Paris service.

text.p: Tunisian state airline, Tunis Air, said it plans to launch a four-times weekly Boeing 737-200 freighter service between Paris and Tunis later this month or early November in partnership with Air France.

At present Tunis Air and Air France each operate a twice-daily passenger service between Paris and Tunis using Airbus 300 passenger aircraft which can carry up to four cargo pallets, a Paris-based Tunis Air cargo official told Reuters.

"With the introduction of winter schedules at the end of the month, Tunis Air is going to switch to an Airbus 320 aircraft and Air France to a 737 passenger aircraft, neither of which can accomodate palletized freight," he said.
"The 737-200Fs which can carry up to seven cargo pallets, will compensate for the loss of bellyhold capacity on the route."
Two of the four freighter flights will operate a Paris/CDG-Tunis rotation and the other two a Paris/Orly- Tunis rotation.

"Using both CDG and Orly will allow for efficient transhipment because a good volume of inbound freight from Tunis is destined to be transferred on to long-haul flights, mainly to North America," the official said.
The 737-200 freighter, owned by Tunis Air, would be available to operate additional frequencies should market demand warrant it, he added
